newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA RAND/BONDS CLOSING REPORT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA RAND/BONDS CLOSING REPORT.

text.p: The rand slipped to its lowest level in more than two months against the British pound on Tuesday after sterling received a boost from a U.K rate hike and news of greater independence for the Bank of England.

However, against the U.S. dollar the rand spent a languid day hovering around overnight levels in moribund trade. At 1412 GMT the rand was at 4.4530/4560 against the U.S. currency from 4.4550/4580 late on Monday.
"The rand/pound is the only story. (Against the dollar) turnover was low. There is no fresh news, no interest, even the bonds are range-trading," a dealer said.
South African bonds, after a strong start, retraced their gains to trade steady in dull late afternoon activity.
"The pound has certainly gone charging ahead on the rate hike and news about the BoE (Bank of England)," a currency trader said.

The rand fell to a worst intraday level of 7.3039 bid against sterling -- its lowest since February 28 when it touched 7.3078 bid -- after newly appointed Chancellor of the Exchequer, Gordon Brown, raised U.K rates to 6.25 percent from 6.20 previously in a bid to tame inflation.

At the same time the new Labour government astounded financial markets by announcing that it would give the Bank of England freedom to set interest rates, a move which pushed the pound to a four-and-a-half yr high against the mark.
At 1412 GMT, the rand had recovered some its composure to trade at 7.2882/2975 against sterling.
Against the other crosses, the rand was last at 0.3869/3872 agains the mark from 0.3883/3887, and at 28.1611/2025 yen from 28.4167/4470 yen previously.
Traders forecast a tight 4.45-4.46 range for the rand against the dollar on Wednesday.
On the bond market, the key R150 was last at 14.825 percent, unchanged from late Monday, and retracing from a firm start when the yield touched an intraday low of 14.715 percent.
Dealers said the drift up in yields, especially in the afternoon, was due to the weaker U.S. 30-year Treasury bond which was last at 6.91 percent from 6.88 before.
"There has also been a bit of talk of foreign selling in the R162's which has led to the spread between the R150's and R160's narrowing," a trader said.
Volumes had been moderate with institutional interest very muted amid an absence of fresh factors and local economic data.
Traders said bonds had received no boost from the many new Eurorand issues announced on Tuesday.
"They were all in the short-end of the market. Either one-, two- or three-years," a dealer said.
They forecast a trading range for the R150 of 14.69-82 percent for Wednesday.

Dealers earlier said Monday's massive net foreign purchase of more than one billion rands worth of bonds was likely to have been an asset swap as it did not move through market, where volumes, epecially from offshore, had been thin.
The Bond Exchange said earlier foreigners were net buyers of 1.052 billion rand's worth of South African bonds on Monday. The Exchange said it could not provide a further breakdown of the purchases.
Nominal cumulative volumes on the bond market on Monday were pegged at 4.92 billion rand from 43.69 billion rand previously.
On the money market major banks kept their three month deposit rates steady at between 16.40 to 16.45 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at between 15.80 to 15.95 percent.
The Reserve Bank said the money market shortage jumped over one billion rand on Monday to 10.256 billion rand from 9.048 billion rand on Saturday.
-- Nicole Mordant, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
